neutral_facts: On the night of 11 January 2000, the victim was last known to be travelling from a town toward his village after an outing. Around 10 p.m., the victim's brother saw the accused near a tubewell and a bus stand, running away with blood-stained clothes; the brother identified the accused in vehicle headlights and did not then know of any killing. The next morning the victim's wife reported that he had not returned home. The family searched and found the victim's body near a water-supply tubewell, lying in a pool of blood, with wounds on the forehead, nose and eyebrows; his shirt, sweater and slippers lay some distance away. Police recorded the body's location, took possession of the body, a blood-stained brick and clothing, and prepared an inquest. A post-mortem recorded multiple injuries, including contusions on the back, a large chest swelling with fractured ribs and blood in the chest cavity, and lacerated wounds on the forehead and above the right eye; the examining doctors stated that these injuries were sufficient to cause death. In the early hours of the next day the accused attended a government hospital, where a doctor recorded a superficial incised wound on the back of the left forearm with a corresponding cut in the shirt. Later, a witness stated that the accused had told him that on the earlier night he had quarrelled with the victim after both drank liquor and had struck him with a brick. On disclosure by the accused, police recovered blood-stained clothes concealed in a wooden box in the accused's house. Forensic analysis found the same blood group ('O') on the recovered clothes and on the victim's clothing.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from multiple head, chest and body injuries; accused had a superficial 22 x 0.2 x 2 to 0.5 cm incised wound on the left forearm
number_of_offences: 1 charged; 0 finally upheld as charged (s.302 set aside; s.304 Part I conviction substituted)
premeditation_planning: No premeditation found; act treated as committed in a sudden fight in heat of passion
key_evidence_accepted: Chain of circumstances: witness saw accused fleeing blood-stained; medical record of forearm wound; extra-judicial confession to PW-12 corroborated by PW-13; recovery of blood-stained clothes; forensic blood-group match
witness_credibility: Court found no reason to disbelieve the chain of circumstances and the PW-12 confession, which was corroborated by PW-13's medical evidence; no defence explanation for the accused's injury
post_offence_conduct: Seen fleeing blood-stained toward a bus stand; sought medical treatment for forearm wound; blood-stained clothes concealed in a wooden box at home; disclosed the incident to PW-12
custody_duration: Appellant said to be in jail; duration not stated
trial_duration: offence: 11.1.2000 (intervening night of 11-12 January 2000); trial judgment: 3.10.2002; High Court: 24.05.2011; Supreme Court: 19.02.2015
legal_representation: Accused/appellant: J.P. Tiwari, Sanjeev Bansal, Praksh Kumar Singh; State/respondent: Nupur Choudhary (for Kamal Mohan Gupta)
investigation_status: FIR registered; charge sheet filed; charge framed under s.302; trial completed with 15 prosecution witnesses
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction affirmed. Supreme Court: s.302 conviction set aside; convicted under s.304 Part I, ten years and fine of Rs.5,000
defence_argument: Circumstances do not complete the chain; no eyewitness; no motive, so the accused could not be said to be the only person who could have committed the crime
legal_principle_applied: Chain of circumstances test; motive need not be proved; intention or knowledge inferred from circumstances; Exception 4 to s.300 IPC
sentencing_rationale: Not stated explicitly; ten-year sentence follows the finding that the act falls under Exception 4 and is punishable under s.304 Part I
judicial_mitigating_factors: Sudden quarrel after both parties drank liquor, scuffle, absence of premeditation; court held the act covered by Exception 4
other_sentence_order: Fine already deposited under lower court orders treated as deposited in compliance with this Court's direction
